teaser: Ever wondered how someone's appearance can tell a story of neglect?
script:
Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wondered how someone's appearance can tell a story of neglect?[break 1s] The phrase is: 蓬头垢面, péng tóu gòu miàn.[break 0.5s] 蓬 (péng) - unkempt or tangled[break 0.5s] 头 (tóu) - head[break 0.5s] 垢 (gòu) - dirt or grime[break 0.5s] 面 (miàn) - face[break 1s] So, 蓬头垢面 literally means 'a head that is unkempt and a face that is dirty', figuratively describing someone who looks messy or neglected.[break 1s] Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s] In ancient China, individuals who were too focused on their studies or work often neglected their personal grooming. As a result, they would appear disheveled, with messy hair and a dirty face. This idiom reflects that state of being so absorbed in one's pursuits that self-care is overlooked.[break 1.5s] Example 1: 他最近一直忙于工作，整个人看起来蓬头垢面。  
He has been so busy with work lately that he looks disheveled and unkempt.[break 1s] Example 2: 她没有时间打理自己，看上去蓬头垢面。  
She hasn't had time to take care of herself and looks messy.[break 1s] Example 3: 在比赛前，他太紧张了，根本顾不上自己的形象，结果蓬头垢面。  
Before the competition, he was so nervous that he forgot about his appearance and ended up looking unkempt.[break 1s] So, 蓬头垢面 means looking messy or unkempt. Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
